## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One fix is needed before merge: `--exclude` does not read its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which the project's CLI flag policy requires for every new flag under `cli/`. The filtering logic itself is covered by the added unit tests and by an end-to-end archive test.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect()` now skips files whose basename matches any of the patterns and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests, and adds a fixture at `tests/fixtures/hostile-review.txt`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, no files are excluded, because the flag uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. Policy at `.claude/skills/cli-flags/reference.md:5` says: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that pass options through the environment cannot use the new flag, and the project's flag contract breaks for its first new flag. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose and document a separator for multiple globs, add an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` entry to `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-set case.
